issues.description: Key-acceptance policy is complected with the keyPressEvent handler instead of being a separable value
issues.detail: The new branch reads config inside the widget's key handler and inlines the logic 'if not use_enter_for_completions and key != Tab: hide+forward'. The accept-key policy is a value (a set of keys that accept a completion) but it is intertwined with event dispatch, hide behavior, and re-dispatch to the textedit. A simpler shape is to compute an `accept_keys` set once (e.g., {Tab} or {Tab, Enter, Return}) from config and let the handler ask 'is this an accept key?'. That separates the policy (data) from the mechanism (event handling).

issues.description: Enter vs Return is not handled — the predicate only excludes Tab
issues.detail: The guard says `not key == Qt.Key_Tab`, which means *every* other key in this branch (including arrow keys, Escape, Backspace if they reach here, and any modifier-laden key) will hide the popup and forward the event when the option is off. The intent is 'Enter/Return should no longer accept'; the code expresses 'anything-not-Tab should bail out'. Those are not the same fact. State the actual policy as data — the set of keys that *accept* — and branch on membership, not on inequality with one key.

issues.description: Config read happens on every keystroke instead of being cached as a value
issues.detail: `self.get_conf('use_enter_for_completions', section='completions')` is called inside keyPressEvent, so the value is re-fetched per event. The fact 'does Enter accept?' is a value that changes only when the user changes the preference; it should be cached on the widget and updated via a config-change signal. This is a small example of place-oriented thinking (ask the config every time) where a value + subscription would be simpler and faster.

issues.description: Negated boolean predicate reads awkwardly and invites bugs
issues.detail: `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` mixes a negated config read with a negated equality. The double negative obscures the rule. A named local — `enter_accepts = self.get_conf(...)` and then `if not enter_accepts and key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter):` — restates the policy in the same words the user sees in the preference. Naming the value is cheap and removes the cognitive complecting.

issues.description: Default flips long-standing behavior off only via opt-out; the question of default was not stated
issues.detail: The default is True (Enter still accepts), which preserves prior behavior — fine. But the deeper question is whether 'Enter accepts completion' is the right default at all given the bug report. That is a product decision that should be named, not left implicit in a config default. Worth a one-line note in the config definition or PR description so the next reader knows the choice was deliberate.

review.summary: The change is small and the intent is sound: let the user opt out of Enter-accepts-completion. But the implementation complects three concerns inside keyPressEvent — reading the config, deciding whether the current key accepts, and dispatching/hiding — and it expresses the rule as 'not Tab' rather than as the actual fact 'Enter and Return no longer accept'. The cleaner shape is to lift the policy to a value (an accept-keys set derived from the preference, cached on the widget, refreshed on config change) and let the handler ask a single question of that value. The default-True choice is reasonable but should be named, not implicit. SIMPLE is within easy reach here; the current patch is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE.
